market_context: United States and Canada; refrigerator ice-maker troubleshooting.
title: Why Is My Ice Maker Not Making Ice?

seo.title: Why Is My Ice Maker Not Making Ice?
seo.meta_description: Check freezer temperature, the ice-maker setting, water supply, and filter before assuming the ice-maker mechanism has failed.
seo.search_intent: Diagnose why a refrigerator ice maker has stopped producing and separate temperature, water-flow, and mechanism problems.

excerpt: If the ice maker is not producing, confirm that it is enabled and the freezer is near 0°F (−18°C). Then check water supply, tubing, and the filter. If those are normal and the unit still will not fill or cycle, it may need service.
content_html:
When an ice maker stops producing, it is easy to assume the mechanism has failed. Often the problem happens before water ever reaches the ice tray: the freezer is too warm, the ice maker is switched off, the filter is restricting flow, or the supply line is kinked.

The cleanest diagnosis follows the process in order: temperature, power or enable setting, water supply, and only then the ice-making mechanism itself.

Make sure the ice maker is actually enabled

Depending on the model, production may be controlled by a wire shutoff arm, physical switch, touch control, or menu setting. It can be turned off accidentally while moving the bin or cleaning.

Check the owner's manual for the exact control on your refrigerator rather than guessing from another model.

Freezer temperature affects every ice-making cycle

If the compartment is not cold enough, ice production can slow or stop. A household freezer should generally hold around 0°F (−18°C) for food storage.

Do not rely only on the control-panel number if performance is in doubt. An appliance thermometer can confirm the actual compartment temperature after it has stabilized.

Use the water dispenser as a clue

If the refrigerator also has a water dispenser and flow is weak or absent there too, look upstream at the household supply, filter, or a kinked line.

Make sure the shutoff valve is open and inspect the tubing without sharply pulling the refrigerator away from the wall. Follow the installation instructions when moving a plumbed appliance.

A filter can restrict flow without stopping it completely

An old, clogged, or incorrectly seated filter may still pass some water while reducing flow enough to produce small hollow cubes or no ice at all.

Whirlpool specifically lists clogged or improperly installed filters as possible causes of low or absent ice production. Use the replacement interval and installation procedure for your exact filter system.

Inspect the bin before blaming the ice maker

Clumped cubes, a block of ice, or a bin that is not seated correctly can interfere with sensing and moving parts. Remove the bin according to the manual and let stubborn ice thaw naturally.

Do not use knives or metal tools inside the mechanism.

New installation? Give the system time

A newly installed refrigerator needs time to cool the freezer, fill water lines, and begin production. Air may also be present in the water system after a filter change.

Your manual will usually state when normal ice production should begin. Judging the machine too soon can turn normal startup into a false diagnosis.

If water still does not enter, stop adjusting random parts

The inlet valve and ice-maker module involve electricity and pressurized water. If the supply is open, tubing is clear, the filter is correct, and water still does not enter the tray, service is the safer next step.

Do not turn undocumented fill screws or alter valves in an attempt to force more water; that can create leaks or overfilling.

Ice production has normal limits

Frequent door opening, removing a full bin at once, or adding a large load of warm food can temporarily slow production because the freezer must recover temperature.

If the machine still makes ice but much less than it used to, compare a full day's production with the specification in the manual.

When to schedule service

Call for service when freezer temperature is correct, the ice maker is enabled, water supply and filter are normal, and the unit still does not fill or cycle. Leaks and repeated mechanical noises also deserve professional diagnosis.

The shape of the cubes is a diagnostic clue

If the machine still makes some ice, look at what it produces. Small, hollow, or incomplete cubes often fit a low-water-flow problem better than a cooling problem. Cubes that partially melt and freeze into a solid mass suggest temperature fluctuation or warm-air entry.

Those clues can keep you from replacing an ice-maker module when the real issue is the filter, supply line, or freezer temperature.

An ice maker needs two conditions before it can do anything else: enough cold and enough water. Confirm those first and you avoid dismantling a mechanism that may not be the source of the problem.

faq.question: What freezer temperature is best for ice production?
faq.answer: Around 0°F (−18°C) is the standard freezer target; a warmer compartment can reduce or stop ice production.

faq.question: Can an old filter stop the ice maker?
faq.answer: Yes. A clogged or incorrectly installed filter can reduce water flow enough to affect ice production.

faq.question: Is it normal for a new refrigerator to take time to make ice?
faq.answer: Yes. It must cool fully and fill the water system before normal production begins.

faq.question: What if the water dispenser is not working either?
faq.answer: Check the household water supply, tubing, and filter first because both functions may share the same flow problem.
